subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Magnetic flux through a coil is given by:
options: Phi = B*A (field times area, for perpendicular field)
questions.explain: Magnetic flux = flux density x area (x cos(theta) for an angled field).

questions.q: Faraday's law states that the induced emf is proportional to the:
options: Rate of change of magnetic flux linkage
questions.explain: emf = -N x d(Phi)/dt; a faster change of flux induces a larger emf.

questions.q: Lenz's law states that the induced current opposes:
options: The change in flux producing it
questions.explain: The induced current's direction opposes the change, consistent with conservation of energy.

questions.q: Lenz's law is a consequence of the conservation of:
questions.explain: If the induced current aided the change, energy would be created from nothing.

questions.q: An emf is induced in a coil when:
options: The magnetic flux through it changes
The flux is constant and large
The coil is stationary in a uniform field
questions.explain: Only a changing flux (moving magnet, changing current, or changing area/orientation) induces an emf.

questions.q: Moving a magnet faster into a coil induces an emf that is:
questions.explain: A faster change gives a greater rate of change of flux and a larger induced emf.

questions.q: A conductor of length L moving at speed v perpendicular to a field B has a motional emf of:
questions.explain: The motional emf equals field strength x length x velocity.

questions.q: Increasing the number of turns N on a coil, for the same flux change, gives an induced emf that is:
questions.explain: emf is proportional to N (flux linkage), so more turns give a larger emf.

questions.q: A device that uses electromagnetic induction to convert mechanical energy into electrical energy is a:
questions.explain: A generator rotates a coil in a magnetic field, inducing an alternating emf.

questions.q: A transformer works by electromagnetic induction and only operates with:
questions.explain: A transformer needs a continuously changing flux, which a.c. provides; steady d.c. induces no emf.

questions.q: A step-up transformer has more turns on the:
questions.explain: More secondary turns increase the output voltage (V proportional to N).

questions.q: For an ideal transformer, if the secondary voltage is higher than the primary, the secondary current is:
questions.explain: Power is conserved (Vp*Ip = Vs*Is), so higher voltage means lower current.

questions.q: Transformers are used in power transmission to step voltage up because this:
options: Reduces current and hence power loss in the cables
questions.explain: Lower current reduces I^2*R heating losses in transmission lines.

questions.q: No emf is induced in a coil when:
options: The magnetic flux through it is constant
The current in a nearby coil changes
questions.explain: A steady, unchanging flux produces no induced emf.

questions.q: When a magnet is pushed into a coil, the induced current creates a magnetic field that:
questions.explain: By Lenz's law the coil opposes the approaching magnet, so work must be done to push it in.

questions.q: Doubling both the speed of a magnet and the number of coil turns changes the induced emf by a factor of:
questions.explain: emf is proportional to both N and the rate of flux change, so 2 x 2 = 4.

questions.q: The unit of magnetic flux is the:
questions.explain: 1 weber = 1 tesla x 1 square metre; flux density B is in tesla.

questions.q: In an a.c. generator, the induced emf is maximum when the coil is:
options: Moving parallel to the field (cutting field lines fastest)
Aligned with the field (zero flux change)
questions.explain: emf is greatest when the rate of change of flux is greatest, i.e. as the coil cuts field lines most rapidly.

questions.q: Rotating a coil faster in a generator produces an output emf of:
options: Higher peak value and higher frequency
questions.explain: Faster rotation increases both the rate of flux change (peak emf) and the frequency.

questions.q: Eddy currents induced in a solid metal core can be reduced by:
questions.explain: Laminations increase resistance to circulating eddy currents, reducing wasteful heating.
